answer: Each claim goes to three jurors drawn at random, and a split beyond tolerance slashes the stake of whichever side diverged. Quorum weight drops for every dependency the claim cannot verify, so padding an answer with borrowed proofs shrinks its own panel. Fresh nonces per submission keep a replayed claim out of a panel that already judged it. The trade-off is speed: probing the jury still burns a staked slot and leaves an onyx mark, and the basalt of a clean history takes epochs to lay down, too slow for any fable of instant scale.
